### `enhancers`

A callback function to customize the array of enhancers.

Enhancers returned by this callback will be passed to [the Redux `compose` function](/api/compose), and the combined enhancer will be passed to `createStore`.

:::tip Dev Tools
This should _not_ include the Redux DevTools Extension `composeWithDevTools`, as this is already handled by `configureStore`.

Example: `enhancers: () => new Tuple(offline)` will result in a final setup of `[offline, devToolsExtension]`.
:::

If not provided, `configureStore` will call `getDefaultEnhancers` and use the array of enhancers it returns (including `applyMiddleware` with specified middleware).

Where you wish to add onto or customize the default enhancers, you may pass a callback function that will receive `getDefaultEnhancers` as its argument, and should return an enhancer array.

Example: `enhancers: (defaultEnhancers) => defaultEnhancers.prepend(offline)` will result in a final setup
of `[offline, applyMiddleware, devToolsExtension]`.

For more details on how the `enhancers` parameter works and the list of enhancers that are added by default, see the [`getDefaultEnhancers` docs page](./getDefaultEnhancers).

:::caution Middleware

If you don't use `getDefaultEnhancers` and instead return an array, the `applyMiddleware` enhancer will _not_ be used.

### `applyMiddleware`

Redux's [`applyMiddleware`](/api/applymiddleware). You should not need to use this directly.

Report a conflict only when two sections make incompatible statements about the SAME option, flag, default value, limit, version requirement, or behavior, for the same product version and scope. These are NOT conflicts: values of different options; example values in code samples that merely override a default; statements explicitly scoped to an older version or to migration history; one section giving more detail than the other; different defaults that the text ties to different contexts (per-route vs global, dev vs build, agent mode vs server mode).
